title: bug: check-dispatch.mjs registers its SIGINT/SIGTERM aborts with process.once, so a second Ctrl+C (or a second TERM) gets Node's default handler and kills the CLI mid-VM-deletion, leaking the check VM
description: scripts/local-runner/check-dispatch.mjs:280 `for (const name of ['SIGINT','SIGTERM']) process.once(name, () => controller.abort())`: after the first signal the listener is gone, so an operator's second console Ctrl+C (which on Windows reaches node directly, and on POSIX reaches the process group) terminates node by default while runCheckJob is still deleting the VM. Repro: start a dispatch whose VM delete is slow, send SIGINT twice; the process exits 130 before the delete completes. Fix idea: keep a persistent listener (process.on) that aborts once and ignores later signals, plus a node --test row. Found in task-e444f6ae's adversarial review; it predates that task.
